sequences.description: Direct endpoint attack: send an unsigned (alg=none) OIDC request object and check whether the authorization endpoint accepts and processes it (proof integrity on request object).

sequences.description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange using a subject_token minted for one upstream connector but validated under a different connector_id (trust anchor substitution). Includes a control exchange to ensure setup is valid.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute any rejection/acceptance in the attack exchange to proof-integrity enforcement (likely setup/grant/connector issue).
Dex accepted a subject_token under the wrong connector_id (trust anchor substitution), indicating verification policy was not applied to the consumed proof.

sequences.description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt to influence consumed identity semantics via id_token_hint during /auth, then verify that the resulting authenticated identity is not derived from the hint without proper verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authenticated session principal matched the victim referenced by id_token_hint, suggesting Dex consumed the hint semantics without applying the intended verification policy to the proof.

sequences.description: Direct-endpoint: attempt to override authorization parameters via an unsigned request object (alg=none) and observe whether the auth endpoint accepts it (proof integrity on request object processing).

sequences.description: Attack: attempt token exchange using a subject_token from one connector context while specifying a different connector_id; verify exchange is rejected (connector binding prevents confused-deputy over-grant). Includes control exchange with correct connector_id.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must be bound to the correct upstream connector trust configuration; a subject token minted under one connector must not be accepted under a different connector_id to gain unintended permissions/claims.
